newsitem.title: USA: GM 1996 Latin America vehicle sales rise.
newsitem.headline: GM 1996 Latin America vehicle sales rise.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Tuesday its vehicle sales in Latin America in 1996 rose 7.5 percent over the 1995 level to a record 541,000 units.

Vehicle industry sales in Latin America trailed 1995 sales during the first half of 1996 but rebounded sharply during the second half of the year to bring 1996 industry sales to a record high of 2.8 million vehicles, GM said in a statement received here.

"GM's robust performance in the region during 1996 continues the strong year-over-year gains in volume and market share that started about six years ago," said Richard Nerod, GM vice president and group executive in charge of Latin America, Middle East and African Operations.
Since that time, GM vehicle sales have more than doubled from some 250,000 units in 1990 to well over 500,000 in 1996.

"Last year was the second year in a row that GM sold over one-half million vehicles in Latin America and, in 1996 alone, GM's market share rose by 1.6 percentage points to 19.2 percent, following the gain of 2.3 percentage points in 1995," he said.
Nerod said GM outperformed the vehicle market in virtually every country with significant market share gains in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay, Colombia, and Ecuador.
GM retained its market leadership position in Chile, Ecuador, Venezuela, and Colombia, he said.

"Looking ahead," Nerod said, "GM is investing in new facilities in the region and expanding our strong dealer network, and remains very positive about the prospects for continued strength in the Latin American market."
